# PCA

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/trippzac/PCA/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/trippzac/PCA/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/trippzac/PCA/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/trippzac/PCA)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of PCA is to recreate the functionality of built-in functions for principal component analysis using my own code.

## Installation

You can install the development version of PCA like so:

```{r}
# devtools::install_github("trippzac/PCA", build_vignettes = T)
```

## Example

This is a basic example of how to use PCA. Its use and output is similar to that
of the built-in function "prcomp".

```{r}
library(PCA)
set.seed(17)
y <- matrix(rnorm(101*10), 101, 10)
PCA(y)
```


I also intend to include some visualization functions and/or other dimension reduction techniques as a part of this package in the future.
